topics.label: Lecture welcome and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience and frames the lecture by stating its subject and learning objectives.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These treatments remove or damage tumors directly, with early detection and treatment alongside surgery shaping their use.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: mechanisms, benefits and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells, their clinical successes, and the toxicity and resistance that limit them.

topics.label: Targeting hormone dependence in breast and prostate cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These treatments inhibit hormone signaling that particular breast and prostate cancers still require for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how defects in checkpoint proteins can make cancer cells vulnerable to irradiation or oncolytic adenoviruses.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking PARP exploits defective BRCA-mediated DNA repair to selectively damage cancer cells.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and genome-guided therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes using cancer-genome information to identify oncogenic drivers on which tumors depend and which targeted drugs might inhibit.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, resistance and chronic disease management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how kinase inhibitors target activated kinases and how off-target effects, resistance and ongoing treatment constrain their benefits.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies for receptor blockade and immune-mediated killing
topics.groupedBecause: These antibodies bind cell-surface targets to block receptor signaling or recruit immune mechanisms that kill cancer cells.

topics.label: Antibody–drug conjugates for targeted cytotoxic delivery
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how an antibody can deliver a linked cytotoxic drug into cells expressing its target.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic weighs the historical and clinical evidence for the immune system protecting against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe reactivating T cells with checkpoint inhibitors and how tumour mutations can provide targets associated with treatment response.

topics.label: T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These approaches bring T cells into contact with tumour targets, either with bispecific engagers or by engineering the T cells themselves.

topics.label: Cancer therapy challenges and personalised treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how biomarkers and cancer sequencing may help match treatments to patients amid resistance and tumour heterogeneity.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and prevention or early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic compares cancer trends while showing how prevention and early detection can contribute to changes in outcomes.

topics.label: Future priorities and ethical dilemmas in cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers future priorities for cancer care and the difficult treatment choices they raise for patients and clinicians.

topics.label: Closing example: childhood leukaemia survival and treatment trials
topics.groupedBecause: This final subtopic closes the lecture with childhood leukaemia survival as an example of treatment success and the challenge of testing new therapies.
